pr_title: Update "Argon" skin gameplay counters to new design
pr_body:
- Closes #18888 
- [x] Depends on ppy/osu-resources#292
- [x] Depends on ppy/osu-resources#295
- [x] Depends on resource bump
- [x] Depends on #25402 (for size serialisation)

This is roughly a big one, containing all the changes necessary to bring the HUD to a similar state with the design (at least for the top side of the screen).

I didn't attempt to split this as this mostly contains new components with as less complexity as possible, but I've organised the changes to allow commit-by-commit reviewing for convenience).

https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/22781491/c043889d-050a-44e3-9a4f-99ec21755c5e

Notes:
 - The combo/accuracy counters should probably be set to fixed-width, but I've kept them as-is to match design, leaving it to others for tweaking it.

 - The argon health display's width is slightly less than the component's actual dimensions, due to the little white bar preceding the health bar.

 - The font size specifications are intentionally different from the reference designs. To be specific, they're set to 1.2x the reference specifications, to remain visually matching with the designs (see https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/issues/3271 & https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/pull/5123).

 - The counters could be given a nice blue-ish tint by bringing the wedges to be on top of them:
   
   https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/22781491/2c854ce4-d78f-492c-a964-6a3ed294f713
 
 - The glyph scale factors has been tweaked to match the reference design at 1x drawable scale (settling at 0.125x).

 - I've intentionally exposed `ArgonWedgePiece` to allow for users to utilise the wedges in their custom "Argon" skins, seeing that there's no harm in doing so.

issue_context.title: Update gameplay HUD visuals
issue_context.body: New HUD designs have been available for some time now. This involves applying the new layout, and also updating pieces which feel pretty jank currently (like the song progress display). May require some extra design effort.
comments: @peppy Since this is included in the project, I've taken a look at it. To start off, should I begin by following each detail in the design provided in figma (i.e. stuff like the decorating lines around the key counter and the song progress)? or should I stick to the main components like the ones at the top left. https://www.figma.com/file/up6guVobzpc3DZlQxWzVmv/Gameplay-Layout?type=design&node-id=2-673&mode=design&t=ZKTQ9MHNwuGj92PN-4 For what it's worth, I've attempted implementing the little details in the key counter and song progress just to see how possible that would be. Not sure if it's agreed having them implemented or not:

I'm not too sure about the line details for now, as they may need to change depending on where the key counter is placed (or at very least need user configuration over their position).

The main goal of the issue is to update the top-centre cluster (score, combo, accuracy) to match argon, so I'd focus on those as a priority.

review_comments: For the record this only kinda works due to `PercentageCounter.FormatCount()` / `FormatUtils.FormatAccuracy()`. You generally cannot and should not be doing such shenanigans with stringed numbers because you might not necessarily know which locale they're formatted in and assuming things about where the dot or percent sign are will end badly.

We might need to reconsider these implementation from a performance perspective in the next profiling round. These string functions can be quite expensive when this text is being updated every update frame.
it's not cpu but memory concerns (which leads to GC etc.) so look at the "allocated" column if anything.
